judgment_text:
Common Prayer: Writ Petitions filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India to praying to issue a writ of certiorari, calling for the records relating to the impugned notice cum order dated 5-3-2026 passed in in Na.Ka. No. 626/224/F1, on the file of the 1st respondent herein, and to quash the same

The Order of the Court was delivered by

S.M. Subramaniam, J.:— Final eviction notice dated 5-3-2026 is sought to be assailed in the present Writ proceedings.

2. The Commissioner, Maduranthakam Municipality received a complaint from one Mr V. Sridhar, 3rd respondent that there is a water channel of Maduranthakam Lake situated on the Southern side of the Hospital Road and Mr Manoharan, S/o. Arumugam, Mr Dhanasekar, S/o. Sundaramoorthy, have encroached upon the said water body and constructed a building.

3. A complaint has been filed for removal of encroachments in the water body. Show cause notice under Section 128 of the Tamil Nadu Urban Local Bodies (Amendment) Act, 2022 [hereinafter referred to as “the Act”] was issued to the petitioners on 7-8-2025. The petitioners submitted a reply in response to the show cause notice on 18-8-2025. The Explanation submitted by the petitioners was considered and final notice was issued on 13-2-2026. Since the petitioners have not vacated from the encroached portion of the water body, the final impugned proceeding has been issued on 5-3-2026.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the classification has been changed and now it is a road poramboke and not a water body.

5. However, the said ground raised deserves no merit consideration from the hands of this Court. If at all any right exists to the petitioners, they have to approach the competent forum. As far as the final notice impugned is concerned, enquiry has been conducted by following the procedures contemplated under the Act and the power of judicial review of the High Court is to ensure the processes through which the decision has been taken by the competent Authorities and not the decision itself. This being the scope of power of judicial review, if the petitioners have any right over the property, they have to approach the competent forum.

6. With these observations, this Writ Petitions stand dismissed. No costs. Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
